steps: Keep the full scan report, scanner version, source revision and scan run together.

Report suspected false positives to the scanner project with the rule, location, intended behavior and a reproducer. For catalog submissions, use the existing submission PR. Do not publish real secrets or private source.
A maintainer must distinguish a detector defect from a source problem, a risky capability or an infrastructure failure.
Scanner maintainers own detector fixes and releases; catalog operators own their pinned scanner updates. Contributors need not maintain a scanner fork.
Keep the score and severity gates unchanged; do not disable rules or trust a submitter-provided baseline.
Repeat the scan on the exact source revision with the reviewed scanner release and unchanged policy. Catalog submissions require a new centralized scan.

components.rationale: Manifest integrity blends existence, JSON validity, required fields, and semver checks.
Path safety uses the scanner's declared-path safety check.
Disclosure is one explicit signal, not a proxy for the entire security posture.
License clarity remains a separate scored signal.
Secret hygiene uses the scanner's hardcoded-secret detection.
Approval hygiene checks for bypass-style defaults.
Documentation reflects README coverage for operators and maintainers.
Manifest metadata tracks the scanner's recommended-metadata check.
Discoverability uses category plus keyword coverage.
Provenance reflects author, homepage, and repository metadata coverage.
Action pinning uses the scanner's immutable-action check.
Permission scope uses the least-privilege workflow check.
Untrusted-checkout protection uses the scanner's privileged-workflow check.
Update automation combines Dependabot coverage and lockfile hygiene.
